children: , the mobile-chip designer, unveiled two 2-nanometer Snapdragon platforms aimed at putting more AI work directly on smartphones. Its shares fell about 1.0% to $196.265 Wednesday morning.

The Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 sits at the top of the lineup, while the 8 Elite Gen 6 brings many of the same AI, camera and connectivity features to a broader range of premium phones. Qualcomm named nine participating brands, including Motorola, OnePlus, Oppo, Vivo and Xiaomi. Motorola has announced a phone using the Extreme chip, giving the launch its first concrete device example.

The investor question is whether two flagship chips can turn more premium phone launches into more sales for Qualcomm. The image adds a valuation check: at $196.265, the shares sit 11.87% above the displayed GF Value of $175.44. That gap puts pressure on the new lineup to deliver more than an impressive launch; device volumes and the appeal of on-device AI will matter next.

title: Qualcomm Falls 1% as Dual 2nm Chips Widen the AI Phone Bet
